subject: Pricing match request + ops carveouts for CloudVertex pilot
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@cloudvertex.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudVertex Procurement <procure@cloudvertex.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor comparison — price match request and ask for onboarding carveouts

Hannah —

Thanks for the time last week. We ran the numbers and EdgeScale has come back with a commercial that materially undercuts Redwood on unit inference cost for our expected throughput (roughly 120M tokens/month).

High level ask: can Redwood match the headline unit price and provide operational carveouts for the pilot? Specifically: a 3-month pilot with waived egress during data migration, and a small onboarding credit to offset migration engineering.

Attached is the EdgeScale term sheet (EdgeScale_Comp_Offer.pdf) — the economics are aggressive but we’d prefer to stay with Redwood if we can get price parity plus the two carveouts above. Procurement is asking for a written proposal by EOD Monday so we can compare apples-to-apples.

Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps — Amit Shah, VP Engineering, CloudVertex.

--
Amit Shah
VP Engineering | CloudVertex
amit@cloudvertex.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@cloudvertex.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor comparison — price match request and ask for onboarding carveouts

Amit —

Appreciate the transparency and for sharing the EdgeScale term sheet. We definitely want to keep CloudVertex on Redwood. Looping in Jordan (pricing & deal economics) and Kim (customer success & onboarding) to scope a practical matching proposal that doesn’t put you at risk and preserves our SLA commitments.

Quick notes from my side:
- We can do a structured price match for the pilot year if we align on minimum commitment profile and usage cadence.
- For the operational carveouts you requested (3-month waived egress + onboarding credit), we typically model the credit as a capped, one-time offset and prefer to tie the waiver to migration milestones so it’s not open-ended.

Jordan / Kim — can you draft numbers that match EdgeScale’s headline while preserving a fallback path for us (e.g., reduced credit if usage doesn’t reach X tokens in month 2)? I’ve attached the basic vendor comparison template we use.

Amit — is procurement expecting a DocuSign-ready SOW or is a redlineable PDF acceptable initially?

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@cloudvertex.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor comparison — price match request and ask for onboarding carveouts

Amit / team —

We pulled together a concise matching proposal and an ops carveout structure so you and procurement can evaluate side-by-side with EdgeScale. See summary below and attached worksheet (redwood_price_match_proposal.xlsx) and a short SOW stub (SOW_pilot_stub.docx).

Summary proposal (high level):
- Headline: Match EdgeScale per-token unit price for first 12 months of the contract, conditional on a 12-month commercial term and minimum monthly velocity of 80M tokens after month 2.
- Pilot carveouts:
  * Waived egress fees for up to 3 months, capped at 50TB total, applied during the migration window.
  * One-time onboarding credit of $25,000 amortized as a bill credit within the first invoice cycle.
- Support: Dedicated onboarding PO (2 weeks) + one named technical contact during migration; standard SLA retained (99.9% uptime).
- Fallback: If monthly usage is < 40M tokens in month 2, onboarding credit reduces to $10k and egress waiver capped at 20TB. This protects both parties from a mis-sized pilot.

Why this structure: it gets you near-term economic parity while preserving predictable unit economics for us. The caps and milestone triggers are intended to be easy for procurement to model.

Amit — we can convert the SOW stub to DocuSign if procurement wants that, or you can review redlines first. If you’re available, I can present the commercial to procurement Monday at 10am PT.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_price_match_proposal.xlsx, SOW_pilot_stub.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@cloudvertex.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 13:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor comparison — price match request and ask for onboarding carveouts

Amit —

I’m Kim on CS/Onboarding. This looks good to me from an operational standpoint — we can staff the dedicated onboarding PO and the technical contact. A few practical notes before you push to procurement:

- Migration timeline: estimate 6–8 weeks to complete migration testing + KV population; waiver should be scoped to the migration window we agree on in the SOW.
- Measurement: we’ll instrument a weekly token/ingest report so procurement can see velocity against the milestone for the credit.
- DocuSign: happy to move the SOW to DocuSign once legal redlines are clear; I’ve put a placeholder DocuSign link in the related_links for procurement convenience.

If all good, Hannah / Jordan — please send the DocuSign-ready SOW (with the caps and fallback language Jordan outlined). Amit — I’ll be on the call Monday when you present to procurement if helpful.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
